articles.title: Bears' Jeffery Simmons Calls Out Lions for 'Crying,' Denies Simulating Jared Goff's Snap Count
articles.summary: Chicago Bears star Jeffery Simmons denied trying to throw off the Detroit Lions offense by mimicking the snap count in Thursday's 39-35 win.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears star Jeffery Simmons denied trying to throw off the Detroit Lions offense by mimicking the snap count in Thursday's 39-35 win.

"I see there's a lot of crying on that side of the ball when that happened," he told reporters after the game. "But as a defensive lineman, when your quarterback checks, I'm allowed to say he can check into a run. When [Lions quarterback Jared Goff] checked, and I said, 'It's a run; they're checking to a run,' it's not my fault your center jumped. That's literally the only time I said something.

"All the other ones, I think he just knew when I'm lined up right up his head; that's on him. He's trying to get to a position (where) he could block me. Just like the one that he fumbled, I'm firing off the ball. At the end of the day, I don't have to cheat, as they say."

Simmons added that he doesn't have to cheat to blow up a play at the point of attack:

The Lions committed four false start penalties in the defeat. Twice in the first half Detroit offensive linemen were flagged on back-to-back snaps.

During the CBS broadcast, three-time Defensive Player of the Year JJ Watt pointed out the fact that Simmons appeared to be a little more vocal than usual as he lined up over the center:

Lions offensive guard Christian Mahogany was more direct, telling reporters he thought the Bears were simulating the snap count.

A defense using disconcerting signals is a 15-yard penalty, but the rule is rarely enforced. ESPN's Kalyn Kahler reported in September 2025 that "it is too difficult for officials to hear through the crowd noise from their positions on the field to call the penalty."

Having this become a storyline on one of the NFL's big showcase days could prompt some sort of reassessment.

The Bears and Lions play again on Jan. 3 in the penultimate week of the regular season. There might be a little more added focus on Simmons pre-snap in the rematch.

articles.summary: 49.ª edición consecutiva en la que los Cowboys acogieron el partido de Acción de Gracias,
articles.body: Jake Elliott, con un 'field goal' de 59 yardas a dos segundos del final, culminó el jueves de Acción de Gracias con una remontada épica de los Philadelphia Eagles, que llegaron a perder por 21 puntos en el tercer cuarto antes de derrotar a los Dallas Cowboys por 38-39. Este resultado entre rivales de la División Este de la Conferencia Nacional deja a los Cowboys (5-7) muy tocados de cara a sus opciones de postemporada, con los Eagles (4-7) todavía últimos del grupo. El 'quarterback' de los Eagles, Joe Milton, que en 2025 militó en los Cowboys, completó 21 de sus 31 pases para 331 yardas, con tres pases de 'touchdown', una anotación por tierra y una intercepción que en ese momento pareció letal. También sufrió cinco 'sacks', para una pérdida de 30 yardas. Por su parte, Dak Prescott, el mariscal de campo de los Cowboys, completó 19 de 28 pases para 291 yardas, con dos pases de 'touchdown', también una anotación terrestre. También sufrió una intercepción y tres 'sacks' para una pérdida de 26 yardas. El 'running back' de los Cowboys Javonte Williams anotó tres 'touchdowns', dos por tierra y uno por recepción, igualando el récord de un jugador de Dallas en Acción de Gracias. Los Cowboys llegaron a ponerse 31-10 a 6:46 del final del tercer cuarto, tras un 'field goal' de Brandon Aubrey. El parcial en los últimos 18 minutos de partido sería de 7-29 para la remontada de Philadelphia, campeones del Super Bowl en 2024. Todo empezó con un espectacular pase de 45 yardas de Milton para el 'touchdown' de DeVonta Smith y el 31-17. En el primer tiempo, Milton ya había lanzado un pase de 50 yardas que Smith atrapó en la zona de anotación de Dallas. Una conexión perfecta. Volvieron a recortar distancia al inicio del último cuarto, con un 'touchdown' de Kenny Moore II, que devolvió hasta la zona de anotación un despeje de los Cowboys bloqueado por los equipos especiales de Philadelphia. Entonces respondió Prescott con un 'touchdown' tras una carrera de 14 yardas y un salto acrobático hasta la zona de anotación. Pero apenas un minuto después, en un 'drive' de solo tres jugadas, Milton replicó la acción de su rival para el 38-30. Los Eagles optaron por buscar la conversión de dos puntos en lugar de patear el punto extra, pero fallaron, una decisión que les pudo salir muy cara. Después llegó la intercepción a Milton en el siguiente 'drive' para Philadelphia y un 'field goal' de 40 yardas fallado por Aubrey. A 2:10 del final, Milton encontró a su 'wide receiver' Makai Lemon para otro 'touchdown' de los Eagles, que, obligados a buscar una conversión de dos puntos, volvieron a fallar y dejaron el marcador en 38-36. Con menos de un minuto en el reloj, Dallas se jugó un cuarto down y una yarda para agotar el tiempo, pero la defensa de Philadelphia derribó a Prescott y dio una última oportunidad a los Eagles, sin tiempos muertos disponibles. La ofensiva de los Eagles le dejó a su pateador, Jake Elliott, la patata caliente de un 'field goal' de 59 yardas para la gloria o el fracaso. Elliott, cuyo récord personal es de 61 yardas, culminó con una patada perfecta una remontada a todas luces épica. "Las cosas no nos estaban saliendo bien en la primera mitad, pero nos mantuvimos unidos y seguimos trabajando poco a poco. Siempre hablamos de cortar leña y cargar agua, y eso es lo que hizo hoy el equipo", explicó tras el partido DeVonta Smith, autor de dos 'TD'. El de este jueves en Dallas fue la 49.ª edición consecutiva en la que los Cowboys acogieron el partido de Acción de Gracias, una de las tradiciones deportivas más arraigadas de Estados Unidos.

articles.body: Mike Tomlin coached the Pittsburgh Steelers for 19 years, and although there was a Super Bowl high and that low earlier this year when he decided to quit, he never presided over something like the Aaron Rodgers vs. Mike McCarthy feud going public the past couple of days. And Tomlin didn't like it. He said the prevailing feeling about the situation now is "just general sadness." And worse. SUPER BOWL-WINNING COACH MIKE TOMLIN LANDS NBC ROLE ON 'FOOTBALL NIGHT IN AMERICA' BROADCAST "I'm upset about it," Tomlin said during a halftime interview with play-by-play voice Mike Tirico on NBC's Sunday Night Football broadcast. "Um, you know, it's a dumpster fire. And I don't say that in a judgmental way. "I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I'm sure, Steelers nation is upset." AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY DISAGREEMENTS AT HEART OF QUARTERBACK'S BENCHING BY THE STEELERS On Tuesday the Steelers announced they were benching Rodgers and making him inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos. On Wednesday, Rodgers responded by going on the "Pat McAfee Show" and claiming McCarthy falls asleep in meetings, snores in those meetings, isn't prepared with the game play as late as Tuesday, misstated what team he coaches while breaking down the team at halftime of a game against the Philadelphia Eagles, and is generally "unwell." Within hours, the Steelers released Rodgers. McCarthy denied falling asleep and missing meetings, and accused Rodgers of presenting him with "an ultimatum" about taking the play-calling away from the coach or he'd ask to be released – something Rodgers confirmed. AARON RODGERS NFL CAREER SEEMS OVER BUT THREE TEAMS COULD CONSIDER QUARTERBACK AS A LATE-SEASON OPTION "I had a range of emotions watching those course of events play out yesterday," said Tomlin, who coached the Steelers from 2007 through last season. "I think the prevailing [feeling] is just general sadness. Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career of the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers. "And just on the macro level, whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum. Those are things that kind of run counter-culture to professional football." Tomlin coached Rodgers last season and it is no secret he respected and admired Rodgers for year before that. That's one reason the Steelers were interested in signing Rodgers last season. But Tomlin said it nonetheless shocked him when Rodgers pulled back the curtain on his feelings for McCarthy on national TV. "It certainly did," Tomlin said. "But, you know, particularly because I know both men involved. Certainly had a lot of intimate work and and development of relationship with Aaron over the last couple of years and have known and competed against Mike, you know, respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time." There has been no Steelers player that either publicly or privately has said what Rodgers said untrue. Tomlin was asked how the quarterback is viewed in the Steelers locker room. "He was beloved, and I'm not, you know, over-exaggerating that," Tomlin said. "He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture, to be engaged with teammates." How? "Particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years, and at times, they lose a little patience for the process," Tomlin said. "Or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys. "Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real natural way." STEELERS TEAM PRESIDENT CHOOSES SIDE IN AARON RODGERS, MIKE MCCARTHY SPLIT So does Tomlin believe McCarthy can effectively lead the Steelers the rest of the way this season after what Rodgers uncovered? THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! And here's a hint to his answer: It's not a definitive yes. "You know, it certainly created some challenges and challenges is probably an understatement if all of those things are true," Tomlin said. "...But his ability to overcome that, or inability to overcome that, in my opinion, is based on relationships." That is an unvarnished view of the situation from someone who lived within that Steelers organization and culture for nearly two decades. It doesn't suggest the Steelers are going to be fine. articles.title: Dak Prescott Reacts to Cowboys' Historic 21-Point Meltdown in Loss to Eagles, 'Pretty Stunning'
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott offered a blunt assessment of Thursday's collapse in a 39-38 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott offered a blunt assessment of Thursday's collapse in a 39-38 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

He called the result "pretty stunning" and compared it to the 33-30 overtime defeat to the Arizona Cardinals.

"I said that about the Cardinals game, but this one takes the cake," Prescott said.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones used the word "numb" to describe his feeling in the immediate aftermath, and Prescott agreed with that emotion.

"It's a good description for how I'm feeling right now, especially this soon after the game, and understanding the plays left out there, the plays could have made, should have made, and the mistakes we had," he said.

The pressure was ramping up on head coach Brian Schottenheimer, and the fan outcry might now be hitting a fever pitch. Prescott didn't exactly give a ringing endorsement of Schottenheimer when asked how he'd feel about a change to the staff:

The four-time Pro Bowler also faced a question about the state of the Dallas defense, which is canceling out the team's dynamic offense for the second successive season:

The sense of déjà vu will be the most frustrating thing about all of this. The Cowboys are falling short in ways that have dogged them for multiple years, be it questionable coaching, a leaky defense, failing to close out games.

There's no immediate remedy, and it's doubtful that firing Schottenheimer would make a difference toward the defense. Sidelining defensive coordinator Christian Parker has done nothing to help the unit.

Dallas can't count on Prescott performing at this level forever. He'll be 34 when the 2027 season kicks off. Once Prescott begins to decline, the franchise could be in serious trouble.

articles.title: Bills Beat Chiefs on FG in Wild Finish, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Mahomes, Allen, Kelce, More
articles.summary: Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills came away with a 13-10 Thanksgiving victory over Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs in Orchard Park, New York, on Thursday.
articles.body:
Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills came away with a 13-10 Thanksgiving victory over Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs in Orchard Park, New York, on Thursday.

The game came down to a last-minute walk-off field goal, as Tyler Bass drilled a 57-yard attempt through the uprights in rainy conditions to secure the win.

The Bills entered the matchup as 3-point favorites over the Chiefs, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

Buffalo's victory solidified its hold on the top spot in the AFC, improving to 10-1 overall and 7-1 in conference play while strengthening its position atop the AFC East standings with their seventh straight win.

The Chiefs fell behind the red-hot Denver Broncos in the AFC West, dropping to 8-3 overall and 6-2 in conference play while holding onto second place in the division and fifth place in the AFC playoff race.

Neither elite quarterback could find the end zone after the first quarter, as the Bills were held to 11 plays and the Chiefs went three-and-out on consecutive possessions.

The Bills struck first in the second, with James Cook III rushing for a touchdown to take a 7-0 lead.

Allen threw his 10th interception of the season, but Kansas City failed to capitalize on the turnover. The Chiefs added a field goal before halftime, trailing 7-3.

Kansas City scored its first touchdown of the game when Emmett Johnson rushed it in for six. Allen then threw his second red zone interception of the game in the rainy conditions, leaving the Bills trailing 10-7 heading into the fourth quarter.

Buffalo's Bass drilled a 54-yard field goal in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 10, but Kansas City's Harrison Butker couldn't match him later in the quarter, missing a 46-yard attempt that would have given the Chiefs the lead.

Both teams struggled to get into field goal range, but a tipped punt by the Bills and a 17-yard return set up Bass for a 57-yard field goal to secure the walk-off victory.

The Chiefs will have the shortest turnaround among the teams playing on Thanksgiving when they face the Los Angeles Rams next Thursday, Dec. 3, at 8:15 p.m. ET, while the Bills will hit the road to face the New England Patriots next Sunday, Dec. 6, at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Bills beat Chiefs on deflected punt, Tyler Bass' 57-yard field goal at the buzzer
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen meet again in Week 12.
articles.body: The Bills overcame a sluggish offensive game in rainy, windy conditions to beat the Chiefs on Thanksgiving in Buffalo, winning 13-10 on Tyler Bass' 57-yard field goal as time expired. The kick came after a Bills defensive stop deep in the Chiefs' own end and a partial block of Matt Araiza's punt. Local hero Joe Andreesen got a piece of Araiza's punt, and Greg Dortch bravely returned it to the Kansas City 39-yard line, setting up Bass' game-winner in an ugly offensive night.It was Buffalo's sixth straight regular-season victory over the Chiefs, dating back to 2021.The Chiefs had a chance to run out the clock in a 10-10 game with less than 30 seconds left, but Patrick Mahomes fumbled the first-down snap, derailing the drive, and Travis Kelce dropped a well-placed pass that likely would have sent the game to overtime. The Bills then deflected Araiza's punt and returned it to the Chiefs’ 39-yard line.The Chiefs also had a huge first-down catch by Rashee Rice controversially wiped out by replay with just under two minutes left that could have tilted the game in Kansas City’s favor.This was ruled a catch for Rashee Rice on the field and was overturned to incomplete after review: pic.twitter.com/mh6QNXsnPJ— Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 27, 2026 The two teams combined for 471 yards of offense in the poor weather, which kept up for the duration of the game. The Bills moved to 10-1, maintaining their lead on the rest of the AFC. The Chiefs fell to 8-3, half a game behind the first-place Broncos in the AFC West.Buffalo increased its probability of winning the conference’s No. 1 seed to 63%, according to The Athletic. Kansas City’s fell to 3%. It was a slog for superstar QBsJosh Allen struggled through one of the poorest passing games of his career, throwing for 81 yards and two interceptions. His legs got the Bills out of some jams, but they mainly had to lean on the running of James Cook, who ran for 117 yards and their only touchdown of the game on 32 carries, which tied his career high.Mahomes, the hotter quarterback coming into the game, had more success Thursday, throwing for 174 yards on 16-of-29 passing. But the Chiefs punted on their first four possessions and came up empty on their final four series, with Harrison Butker's missed field goal with just over six minutes left looming large.The first half was a mess — cold, rainy, windy — and a stark contrast to the high-scoring first two games on Thanksgiving. Both teams traded a pair of punts in a scoreless first quarter. The Bills struck first, laboring down the field to get in the end zone on Cook's 5-yard run, overcoming an overturned TD and a questionable false-start call at the goal line.Buffalo's suddenly hot defense took advantage of the elements and KC’s four straight punts to open the game. It appeared that the Bills would take a two-score lead as they drove to the Chiefs’ 9-yard line, but Allen's pass was tipped by George Karlaftis and intercepted in the end zone by Alohi Gilman to thwart that drive. Gilman PICKS OFF Josh Allen in the end zone.Touchback, Chiefs ball!KCvsBUF on NBC/PeacockStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2DZvaGexOW— NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 The Chiefs finally got going before halftime, driving to the Bills' 8-yard line, but Mahomes' end-zone pass to Rice was incomplete, and the Chiefs settled for a short Butker field goal to cut Buffalo's lead to 7-3.Kansas City came out of halftime with renewed focus, looking the best they had offensively all game. Emmett Johnson, starting again for an injured Kenneth Walker III, capped the drive with a 1-yard TD run. It was an impressive drive despite the rain continuing to fall, giving the Chiefs a 10-7 lead. It was Johnson's fifth straight game with a touchdown. That score ended a streak of 49 drives without allowing a TD by the Bills' defense.Allen, who had only 41 first-half passing yards, was working through his issues gripping the ball, and the Bills penetrated the Chiefs' red zone on their opening drive of the third quarter. But Allen's on-target pass to Khalil Shakir deflected off his hands and went down as Allen's second interception, this time by Nohl Williams.The Bills' defense muscled up again and pushed the Chiefs back, giving Buffalo good field position again. Another labored drive — its fifth of the game of at least four minutes — bogged down, as the Bills had to settle for Bass' 54-yard field goal, tying the game at 10-10.Mahomes was under fire on the ensuing drive, but he completed a third-and-15 pass under heavy pressure — vintage Mahomes — throwing back against his body for 19 yards and a clutch first down. MAHOMES FROM ACROSS THE FIELD.KCvsBUF on NBC/PeacockStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tTzYllktWt— NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 But penalties were a problem all game for the Chiefs, and consecutive flags pushed them back 15 yards. The Chiefs settled for a Butker field-goal try from 46 yards, but he pushed it to the right for his eighth miss of the season. That is two more than he's had in any single season in his 10 years as a Chief. “I’m not going to make any decisions,” Reid said when asked about Butker’s struggles, according to The Athletic’s Nate Taylor. The Chiefs' defense showed it could flex its muscles, too. After Cook moved the chains, the Chiefs sacked Allen just as the Bills moved into Kansas City territory. It was that kind of night for the offense and for Allen.Backed up inside his own 10, Mahomes hit Rice with an 11-yard pass on third-and-10, taking a big hit from the Bills' Amani Hooker. But the play was reviewed, and it was determined that the ball came loose and touched the ground, forcing the Chiefs to punt.Allen got the ball back at his 47-yard line with plenty of time to mount a game-winning drive but had a first-down completion wiped out by penalty and took a massive sack on third down, and the Bills punted with less than 40 seconds left in regulation. Instead, the Chiefs watched the Bills pull out the ugly game in the waning seconds.

articles.summary: The Kansas Chiefs have a kicker problem. Still.

The Kansas Chiefs have a kicker problem. Still.

Harrison Butker missed a 46-yard-field goal attempt in the fourth quarter of Thursday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills, a hugely impactful moment in the 13-10 loss. It was the kicker's eighth miss of the season in 23 attempts.

After the game, head coach Andy Reid addressed the situation:

The Chiefs have abstained from replacing the kicker to this point despite his struggles this season. How much longer they can ignore the issue was a major point of conversation following his Thanksgiving miss:

There wasn't much margin for error during Thursday's game given the wet and wintry conditions, and the difference in kicking quality ultimately was one of the separators. Tyler Bass was 2-for-2 on field goals, both of them over 50 yards, including a 57-yard game-winner as time expired.

articles.title: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni pulled back from fans after Thanksgiving win over Cowboys, team claims he was celebrating
articles.summary: Emotions were high following the Eagles' comeback win over the Cowboys on Thanksgiving.
articles.body:
Emotions were high following the Philadelphia Eagles' comeback win over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving . Especially for Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni.

The immediate aftermath of the game saw Sirianni approach a group of field-level Eagles fans and exchange some high-fives, before looking at another group and getting pulled back by a pair of staffers. It's unclear what happened, but Sirianni appeared to maintain eye contact with someone and tried to force his way back before getting pulled to the field.

It was only a few seconds, but it drew attention on social media.

The simple explanation appeared to be Sirianni, who wears his heart on his sleeve in the best of times, was trying to get into it with the opposing fan base. The team and coach are claiming that wasn't the case.

While speaking with reporters postgame , Sirianni said he was only trying to celebrate with Eagles fans and that he was pulled back to the field to shake hands with Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer:

"There were a lot of Eagles fans back there, I was excited to celebrate with those Eagles fans and our team and everything like that. It was fun … I'm sure there were some [Cowboys fans] in there but at that point it felt like there was only Eagles fans, we were able to high-five. "I had to shake everybody's hand out on the field and wanted to be able to celebrate with everybody, and also shake Schotty's hands and their players' hands."

"There were a lot of Eagles fans back there, I was excited to celebrate with those Eagles fans and our team and everything like that. It was fun … I'm sure there were some [Cowboys fans] in there but at that point it felt like there was only Eagles fans, we were able to high-five.

"I had to shake everybody's hand out on the field and wanted to be able to celebrate with everybody, and also shake Schotty's hands and their players' hands."

An Eagles representative apparently backed up this account with Pro Football Talk , contending that Sirianni was only celebrating. We'll see if anything else comes of that, but Sirianni is the head coach with less to worry about following that game .

Philadelphia's win went down as the biggest comeback in NFL Thanksgiving history. The Cowboys led 28-10 at halftime and by as many as 21 points late in the third quarter, only for a superb performance by former Cowboys practice-squad QB Joe Milton, now playing for the Eagles, and some brutal mistakes by Dallas to trigger a wild comeback.

Eagles kicker Jake Elliott made a 59-yard field goal for the win, improving the Eagles' record to 4-7 in what has been a trying season for a team that won a Super Bowl less than two years ago.

articles.title: Josh Allen Says He'll Be 'Better' After 81-Yard, 2-INT Performance in Bills' Dramatic Win vs. Chiefs
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen knows a performance like he had on Thanksgiving Day won't cut it for his team to remain a Super Bowl contender.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen knows a performance like he had on Thanksgiving Day won't cut it for his team to remain a Super Bowl contender.

Following a 13-10 win over the Kansas City Chiefs, Allen said he's "thankful" for a number of people including his defense, offensive line, kicker Tyler Bass and running back James Cook III.

The 2024 NFL MVP added his level of play wasn't where it needed to be in either of the last two weeks:

Allen went 10-of-21 for 81 yards and two interceptions through the air. Both his picks came inside the red zone, costing Buffalo some valuable points.

The conditions in Buffalo weren't conducive to a lot of offense. Allen called it "one of the grossest weather games I think I've ever played." Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes had 174 yards through the air on 29 attempts.

Still, Allen acknowledged he didn't manage the game well, and turnovers have been a problem for him. He now has 11 interceptions, his most since 2023.

The Bills are more than a one-man show, but their championship hopes rest squarely on Allen. Even in wet, windy conditions, there won't be many more times when Buffalo can afford to have him throw for fewer than 100 yards and come out on top in the end.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes' wife Brittany loses patience with NFL referees after Chiefs suffer another frustrating defeat: "That was the weakest call I have ever seen"
articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes had another reason to be frustrated after the Kansas City Chiefs suffered a narrow 13-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes had another reason to be frustrated after the Kansas City Chiefs suffered a narrow 13-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving. Patrick Mahomes and his teammates struggled to find their rhythm in the rain at Highmark Stadium, but a controversial fourth-quarter decision involving wide receiver Rashee Rice drew an angry response from Brittany. The Chiefs had already faced a significant penalty disadvantage, and the overturned catch added to the frustration. Brittany made her feelings clear on social media, continuing a pattern of publicly questioning officiating after Kansas City's recent defeats.Brittany Mahomes takes aim at referees after controversial Rashee Rice callThe biggest talking point came when Patrick Mahomes found Rashee Rice on third down. The play was initially ruled a catch, but officials overturned the decision following a review. The ruling quickly became a source of frustration for the Chiefs, particularly with the game still within reach.Brittany, who is expecting her fourth child with Patrick, was watching from away from the stadium. She took to Instagram Stories to express her anger over the decision.“HAHAHAHAHA WHAT A JOKE. Guess we can’t even play football without getting it called against us… not sure what an actual catch is after that I guess? I don’t wanna hear [expletive] anymore from anyone.”She did not stop there. The Kansas City Current co-owner also shared her reaction on X, where she described the decision as one of the worst calls she had seen.“THIS IS ONE OF THE WORST CALLS OF ALL TIME.”The numbers added another layer to the debate. Kansas City had been flagged eight times for 86 yards before the disputed play, while Buffalo had received only two penalties for 15 yards. That difference became part of the conversation as fans questioned whether the officiating had been consistent.There was no clear agreement among viewers, either. One fan defended the officials, writing on X, “I mean it’s clear… The ball hits the ground and moves. Clearly not a catch by Rashee Rice.”Another disagreed strongly, arguing that Rice had maintained control even as the ball touched the ground.“Rashee Rice 100% had firm control of the ball when it hit the ground. It didn’t move a single bit. Game changing phantom call from the refs and the worst part is New York reviewed it AND STILL GOT IT WRONG.”The disagreement reflected how much attention the decision attracted, although the overturned call was not the only issue Kansas City faced in the 13-10 defeat.Brittany Mahomes had questioned officiating after Broncos lossThis was not the first time Brittany had publicly criticised referees following a Chiefs defeat this month. Kansas City also suffered a 28-14 loss to the Denver Broncos, with another penalty involving a potential touchdown drawing her attention.Patrick appeared to connect with Rice for what could have been a game-changing score, but officials called a holding penalty on Jaylon Moore, wiping out the play.Brittany reacted on Instagram Stories, writing, “You can’t tell me you call that on a game winning TD, oh wait yeah I can cause it’s us. That was the weakest call I have ever seen, you can’t tell me otherwise.”Head coach Andy Reid also expressed his frustration with the decision, although he stopped short of directly criticising the officials.“I didn’t see it,” Reid said. “I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see [a false start].”Reid also pointed to the team's discipline as a problem after the Denver game. Kansas City committed 11 penalties for 105 yards, compared with Denver's six penalties for 45 yards.“I thought the guys battled like crazy. We had over 100 yards in penalties. We’ve got to take care of that,” Reid added.The latest defeat against Buffalo has added to the Chiefs' concerns. Kansas City still holds a 4-0 playoff record against Josh Allen's team, but its regular-season results tell a different story, with just one win in seven meetings.For Brittany, the frustration is no longer tied to one disputed decision. articles.title: Buffalo Bills 13-10 Kansas City Chiefs: Tyler Bass hits 57-yard field goal in final seconds to snatch victory over NFL rivals
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills beat rivals Kansas City Chiefs thanks to a 57-yard field goal from Tyler Bass; he also hit a 54-yard field goal to level the game with 12 minutes remaining
articles.body:
James Cook had 117 yards rushing and scored on a five-yard run and Bass also made a 54-yard field goal in the defensive struggle.

The highly anticipated fireworks between Buffalo's Josh Allen and Kansas City's Patrick Mahomes, two of the NFL's best quarterbacks, and top offenses failed to materialise.

Allen finished 10 of 21 for 81 yards with two interceptions - both coming inside the Kansas City 20. Mahomes finished 16 of 29 for 174 yards.

Buffalo have won seven straight and matched their best start to a season since 1991.

Emmett Johnson had 72 yards rushing and scored on a one-yard run for the Chiefs.

Neither offense could muster much momentum with rain falling through the evening and cold gusts that made it feel like -5.

Bass's decisive kick came after the Chiefs went three-and-out at their own 11 with 15 seconds remaining. Matt Araiza's punt was partially tipped by Joe Andreessen, leading to a line-drive ball fielded by Greg Dortch, who returned it 17 yards to Kansas City's 39 with four seconds remaining.

Bass's 54-yard field goal to tie it at 10 some 12 minutes earlier also was struck in the same direction.

Kansas City's Harrison Butker, kicking in the other direction toward the north end of the stadium, missed a go-ahead 46-yard attempt wide right with just over five minutes remaining.

In their seventh regular-season meeting since 2020, the Bills improved to 6-1, including six straight wins over Kansas City. The Chiefs, however, hold a 4-0 edge in the playoffs, including two AFC championship game wins.

After Cook opened the scoring 28 seconds into the second quarter, Allen squandered a chance to build a 14-0 lead on the Bills next possession. Facing second-and-eight at the Chiefs nine, Allen rolled to his right, appeared to have his pass slightly tipped by George Karlaftis, and intercepted by Alohi Gilman in the end zone.

It marked the first time in 43 drives inside an opponent's 20 the Bills failed to come away with points this season.

He would turn it over again in the red zone two drives later on Buffalo's first possession of the second half. On first-and-10 at Kansas City's 14, Allen's sidearm pass to Khalil Shakir was low, glanced off the receiver's hands and deflected into the arms of Nohl Williams.

Allen has five touchdowns versus seven interceptions in his past five starts.

The Chiefs continue to face questions over whether they have padded their record with weaker opponents. Of their eight wins, only one - a season-opening victory against Denver - has come against an opponent with a winning record entering Week 12. Meantime, all three losses have come against winning teams.

The Bills, meanwhile, were coming off a four-game stretch in which they feasted in playing against backup and third-string quarterbacks.

Buffalo limited the NFL's best offense to 241 yards and contained Mahomes, who entered the outing combined for 13 TDs passing and averaging 309 yards over his past four games.

Buffalo did allow their first touchdown in four outings, dating to to Derrick Henry's two-yard run in a 36-10 win over Baltimore on November 1. They were also limited to a season-low 230 yards.

articles.title: ‘He Should Straight-Up Refuse to Play Unless They Trade Him’ — Cowboys Fans React as Former QB Questions If Dak Prescott Should Pull an Aaron Rodgers
articles.summary: Turkey is usually the hardest thing to digest on Thanksgiving, but the Dallas Cowboys served up something far heavier on Thursday, inexplicably coughing up a...
articles.body:
Turkey is usually the hardest thing to digest on Thanksgiving, but the Dallas Cowboys served up something far heavier on Thursday, inexplicably coughing up a 21-point lead in a 39-38 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium.

Former Cowboys backup quarterback Ben DiNucci turned the spotlight onto Dak Prescott, questioning how much longer the franchise quarterback would tolerate Dallas' struggles.

Ben DiNucci Weighs in on Dak Prescott's Future After Cowboys Let 31-10 Lead Slip Away

Dallas led 28-10 at halftime and 31-10 after Brandon Aubrey's 59-yard field goal with 3:35 left in the third quarter, only for Philadelphia to score 29 of the game's final 36 points. That run included Kenny Moore II's touchdown return of a blocked punt early in the fourth and ended with Jake Elliott's 59-yard field goal with two seconds left.

Speaking afterward, Prescott measured it against a 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals earlier this month. "Yeah, it's pretty stunning. I said that about the Cardinals game, but this one takes the cake." Asked whether this team is capable of bouncing back, Prescott replied, "We'll see."

DiNucci posed his question later Thursday night, after the loss, writing, "In all seriousness, at what point does Dak say I've had enough?"

One fan answered the question with two simple words: "Very soon."

Another fan hoped for an offseason exit and pointed the finger beyond the field. "I hope it's this offseason. He deserves so much more from a front office," the fan wrote .

Another supporter thought that moment had already passed and wanted Prescott to force a trade soonish. "It should've been after last season. He should straight up refuse to play unless they trade him."

Waiting for the offseason was too slow for one fan, who had landing spots in mind. "Tonight he should pull an Aaron Rodgers and bounce. He will waste another year there next year if he stays … I'm off to the Vikings or Raiders next year if I'm him."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Others doubted that Prescott could force his way out even if he tried, with one fan pointing back to Rodgers. "Look what they did to Rodgers when he did it. The Shield will always protect their own."

For one fan , the money stood in the way. "He could say it tonight and it wouldn't matter. The cap hit is way too high; he's here until '28."

Dak Prescott's Contract Runs Through 2028 With a Full No-Trade Clause

Prescott's contract does run through the 2028 season. He signed a four-year, $240 million extension in September 2024 that came with $231 million guaranteed and a full no-trade clause, which means any trade would need both the Cowboys and Prescott on board.

Dallas has since restructured the deal twice, converting $45.75 million of his 2025 salary and $38.2 million of his 2026 salary into bonuses, and his cap hit is set to jump from about $43.5 million this season to more than $76 million in 2027 and more than $86 million in 2028. He is slated to reach free agency in 2029, the year he turns 36.

BUILD YOUR TEAM'S DRAFT: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Parting ways would not come cheap for Dallas, either. Spotrac lists nearly $130 million in dead money tied to the deal this season and flags 2028 as a potential out, when that figure would fall to about $72.5 million.

His $45 million salary for 2027 is already fully guaranteed, and $17 million of his 2028 salary becomes fully guaranteed early in the 2027 league year. The deal also carries a no-tag clause.

On the field, Prescott finished Thursday 19-of-28 for 291 yards with two touchdown passes and an interception, plus a 14-yard touchdown run, after coming into the game second in the NFL in both passing yards (3,049) and touchdown passes (25).

The loss left Dallas without back-to-back wins since Nov. 27, 2025, and the Cowboys, now 5-7 and third in the NFC East, get an extended break before visiting the Seattle Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7, the first of five regular-season games left.

articles.body:
Thanksgiving night in Orchard Park handed the Kansas City Chiefs a last-second 13-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills, and it served up another helping of the NFL's favorite talking point: an argument over what does and doesn't constitute a catch.

However, this one drew in Kansas City Mayor Quinton Lucas, who chose to treat the replay reversal of a late Rashee Rice catch like a case on appeal.

Mayor Quinton Lucas Rips Refs After Chiefs' Loss to Bills

Writing about the overturned catch, Lucas put it this way: "The failure isn't the review call; it's failure to adhere to the proper standard of review for appeal: 'Clear and incontrovertible evidence' of error. Lawyers know. A close call shouldn't be overturned absent clear error on the initial call. It didn't exist here."

The play he was writing about came with less than two minutes left in the fourth quarter. On third-and-10 deep in Kansas City territory, Rice absorbed a big hit and held on to a Patrick Mahomes throw over the middle, and the officials on the field ruled it an 11-yard completion that moved the chains.

That's when New York decided to step in. Replay officials at league headquarters stopped play just as the Chiefs were snapping the ball again, and the review turned the catch into an incomplete pass.

Kansas City was left facing fourth down deep in its own territory instead of a fresh set of downs. The Chiefs punted, had to punt again before those final two minutes ran out, and watched the Bills win it at the last second.

Mark Butterworth, the NFL's vice president of instant replay, laid out the league's reasoning for pool reporter Matt Derrick. "As the receiver is going to the ground, he had the ball in his right hand and when he contacted the ground, his hand slid up the ball, and we deemed that a loss of control."

Andy Reid, Rashee Rice Push Back on Overturned Catch

Rice didn't need many words to make his case. Asked after the game whether he caught the ball, the receiver answered, "Yes, I did."

Head coach Andy Reid also disagreed with New York's decision to overrule the crew on the field. "I'm not quite sure what they saw. I saw he had control of the ball, and his elbow hit, then the ball hit.

"Normally, in those kinds of situations, it's got to be clear and obvious. And to me, that was not clear and obvious," Reid said.

Mahomes was more careful with his verdict. "I thought from my angle when I threw the ball, I thought his hand was under the ball, but I haven't seen the replay, so I can't put too much into it." His wife, however, decided not to pull any punches in a no-holds-barred rant on Instagram.

Cincinnati Bengals legend Chad Ochocinco, meanwhile, took the complaint beyond this one play. "We have this issue every single week with the referees on what is called a catch. Every week it's something different. That's a catch. I'm not sure what the NFL is doing."

The Bills now improve to 10-1, strengthening their grip on the AFC's No. 1 seed, as the Chiefs fall to 8-3, occupying the conference's No. 5 seed.
